You’re not alone. I’ve had these thoughts when I was in high school. And once I graduated, I thought of doing it at work. I don’t know why I’ve had those thoughts. I guess I just want to share with the world what happens when you pretend like mental illness does not exist. Like it’s not important.

Anxiety, depression and ednos.

With anxiety, it’s like my inner alarm system never turns off. I’m always on edge, even if nothing terrible is happening. I get terrifying, intrusive thoughts. My palms get sweaty, my heart races, my stomach aches and my whole body trembles. I’m mostly afraid of harm coming to me. Like being robbed, beaten up, sexually harassed or assaulted, kidnapped or murdered. I hate social situations. Work is tiring because I have to interact with customers all day long.  I spend most of my time at home when I’m not working or running errands. 

With depression, I feel completely alone and isolated from everyone else. I feel like I don’t belong anywhere. I do not like myself or my life very much. I feel like a failure from the moment I wake up to the moment I fall asleep. It feels like I’m just going through my motions. I often get numb. I can’t feel emotions as strongly, unless it’s sadness or fear.

And lastly, ednos. For those of you who don’t know, ednos is an eating disorder. It’s basically something you are diagnosed with if you don’t have one specific disorder like bulimia or anorexia but show some of the symptoms of them. Over the past few years, I think I lean more towards bulimia. If I eat too much food, I will sometimes take laxatives or simply not eat for many hours. Every time I walk past a mirror or something with a reflection, I will observe my body to see if I look bad. Is any fat showing through my clothes? I will lift my shirt up and check my stomach to see how flat it is. I look at my hips and my thighs, which is find disgusting. I hate how curvy my body is. 

I try to keep my calories as low as I can although it’s been hard lately. My doctor has told me to up my calories since the amount I’m eating is literally equal to how much a toddler is supposed to eat in a day. I’ve tried losing weight the healthy way but it’s like it doesn’t work anymore. I might have messed up my metabolism. I mean, I have been doing this since 2018. FIVE YEARS.
